items.title: Urine test could speed up bladder cancer diagnosis in patients with haematuria
items.summary: A non-invasive urine test could speed up diagnosis of bladder cancer, an NHS study has found. Trials of the GALEAS urine bladder test across seven NHS sites found it discovered nine in ten patients with the disease.

items.title: Womb cancer tests could be used in primary care
items.summary: A test to rule out womb cancer in women who experience bleeding after menopause could be used in primary care, a study has found. items.title: Life-extending breast cancer drug approved for NHS following price deal
items.summary: NICE has finally recommended the life-extending breast cancer drug Enhertu for routine NHS use after reaching a new commercial arrangement.

items.title: Suspected cancer among 44k ‘rejected referral’ letters never sent to GPs
items.summary: Health officials in Northern Ireland are investigating whether any patients have come to harm, as an issue with undelivered letters from hospitals to GPs was revealed be of a much greater scale than initially thought.

items.title: Cardiovascular disease linked to higher risk of cancer death
items.summary: People with cardiovascular disease are more likely to develop cancer and die from the disease than those without cardiovascular conditions, a new study has found. Researchers from the universities of Aberdeen and Keele analysed data from 22,534 people over more than 25 years.

items.title: Supervised exercise programme shows benefit for prostate cancer in NHS trial
items.summary: A supervised exercise programme can counter adverse effects and boost quality of life in men being treated with androgen deprivation therapy for prostate cancer, an NHS trial has shown. Results from the large randomised controlled trial also showed it is costs effective and is easily scalable across the NHS.
